summary: Calendly sells per-seat meeting software: a free scheduling tier, Standard and Teams plans at $10 and $16 per seat per month billed yearly, and an Enterprise plan starting at $15k a year for 50 seats. Between July and October 2026 it stopped selling itself as "Free Online Appointment Scheduling Software" and relaunched as an AI meeting-management platform, adding a Notetaker, an AI assistant called Callie and built-in payments, with Notetaker and Callie sold through Standard Plus and Teams Plus at $18 and $24 per seat. Organic search is the largest channel this capture can measure — DataForSEO estimates about 276,000 monthly US visits, 69% of top-keyword traffic branded — with a product-led free signup as the main conversion and a "Talk to sales" path for larger teams. Paid advertising looks small: LinkedIn is the only platform where the company's own ads were found, Meta shows no active ads, and no Calendly-named advertiser appears in Google's Ads Transparency Center despite a Google Ads tag on every captured page.

business_model.text: Calendly sells per-seat subscriptions across four tiers: a free plan, Standard at $10 per seat per month, Teams at $16, and Enterprise starting at $15k a year.

evidence.detail: Plan cards read "Free" / "Always free", "Standard" $10 "/seat/mo", "Teams" $16 "/seat/mo" and "Enterprise" "Starts at" "$15k" "/yr"
JSON-LD Offers: "Standard Plan (USD)" price 10, "Teams Plan (USD)" price 16, both with unitText "seat/month"

business_model.text: The prices shown by default are annual rates; paying monthly costs $12 and $20 per seat.

evidence.detail: Clicking "Billed monthly" on the pricing page changed the plan cards to $12 and $20
JSON-LD priceSpecification for the Standard and Teams offers carries billingDuration "P1Y", and the cards show "Save 17%" and "Save 20%"

business_model.text: The new AI products are sold as a packaging upgrade rather than a separate add-on: turning on Notetaker and Callie switches the plans to Standard Plus at $18 and Teams Plus at $24 per seat per month.

evidence.detail: Clicking "Add Notetaker & Callie" renamed the tiers to "Standard Plus" and "Teams Plus" at $18 and $24 "/seat/mo", with Notetaker shown as "Included" and the banner reading "Save up to 25%"
With the toggle off, the same Standard and Teams cards carry "Add Notetaker & Callie" and list Notetaker as "Not included"

business_model.text: The AI packaging raises the list price of a paid seat by 80% on Standard ($10 to $18) and 50% on Teams ($16 to $24), which makes existing paid users, not new signups, the most likely source of near-term revenue growth.

evidence.detail: The Plus cards read "$18" and "$24" per "/seat/mo" against "$10" and "$16" without the add-on
The pricing page H1 is "Add Notetaker and Callie to  Standard or Teams plans", an upgrade prompt rather than a plan comparison

business_model.text: Headline per-seat list prices have not moved in nearly two years, so the Plus tiers are where the price increase went.

evidence.detail: The 1 January 2025 pricing copy already shows "$10" and "$16" under a "Billed monthly" / "Billed yearly" toggle, with Enterprise "Starts at" "$15k"
The live page captured for this report shows the same $10, $16 and $15k figures

business_model.text: The motion is hybrid: self-serve through Teams, sales-led at Enterprise, with the handover pinned to a 50-seat floor.

evidence.detail: Free, Standard and Teams carry a "Get started" button while Enterprise carries "Talk to sales" and the note "Starts at 50 seats"
The sales form's qualifying question "How do you plan on using Calendly?" offers seat bands up to "Across departments or multiple teams (50+ users)"

business_model.text: Pricing is published in three currencies as separate list prices rather than as a converted figure.

evidence.detail: JSON-LD offers list Standard at 10 USD, 8 GBP and 10 EUR, and Teams at 16 USD, 13 GBP and 16 EUR

business_model.text: Whether Calendly takes a cut of the payments its customers collect is unknown.

evidence.detail: The Payments rows name "Collect payments at booking via Stripe and PayPal" and "Send invoices for project-based work" but no processing fee or revenue share is stated

positioning.text: Calendly now claims the category of AI meeting management alongside scheduling, with the homepage promising that the whole job around a meeting is handled.

evidence.detail: H1 "All the work around meetings, handled." above a section labelled "AI MEETING MANAGEMENT" with the heading "Built for people whose work runs on meetings"
Title tag "Meeting Scheduling Software and AI Meeting Tools | Calendly"

positioning.text: The repositioning happened between 1 July and 1 October 2026 and replaced a pitch that had been stable for at least eighteen months.

evidence.detail: The 1 July 2026 copy still carries the title "Free Online Appointment Scheduling Software | Calendly" and the body line "Calendly makes scheduling simple"
The 1 October 2026 copy carries the new title and the H1 "All the work around meetings, handled."

positioning.text: The homepage still leads on scheduling leadership, which reads as using the existing market position as the entry point to the AI story rather than replacing it.

evidence.detail: The first product section is headed "Book meetings with the world’s #1 scheduling tool", followed by Callie, Notetaker and Payments sections

positioning.text: Social proof on the public site shifted from organisation counts to raw scale, with the Fortune 500 claim moved off the homepage onto the enterprise page.

evidence.detail: The January 2025 homepage read "Trusted by more than 100,000 of the world’s leading organizations" and "including 86% of the Fortune 500 companies"
The current proof block reads "People using Calendly" "50M+", "Countries with monthly active users" "240+" and "Meetings booked with Calendly" "1.3B+"
The enterprise page carries "Calendly powers scheduling for over 4 out of 5 Fortune 500 companies."

positioning.text: The relaunch has not reached the rest of the site: the enterprise page, the comparison hub and the founder's own bio still carry the old pitch and old numbers.

evidence.detail: The enterprise page still uses the retired tagline "Easy scheduling ahead" as a section heading
The newest post on the "Compare Calendly" hub is dated "May 9, 2025"

positioning.text: Calendly's four biggest organic rivals are not the tools its comparison hub positions against.

evidence.detail: The 12 featured stories include a cat rescue, a pet care business, a jewelry designer, three coaches and a nonprofit

section_summaries.business_model: Per-seat SaaS with a free tier, $10–$16 a seat billed yearly and a $15k-a-year enterprise floor at 50 seats. List prices have not changed since early 2025; the AI relaunch monetises through Plus tiers at $18 and $24, an 80% and 50% uplift on an existing paid seat.
section_summaries.positioning: Calendly has reframed itself from the #1 scheduling tool into AI meeting management, promising that "All the work around meetings" is handled. The new story reaches the homepage and pricing page but not the enterprise page, comparison hub or CEO bio, which still carry the old pitch.
section_summaries.acquisition: Acquisition looks like brand and organic search rather than paid: roughly 276k estimated US visits a month, 69% of top-keyword traffic branded and 73% landing on the homepage. LinkedIn carries the only ads found, Meta and Google show none, and every open job is in engineering, product or security.
section_summaries.funnel: One free-signup funnel built on Google and Microsoft OAuth, with a 14-day Teams Plus trial merchandised alongside the free account, plus a five-field sales form gated on seat count. Marketo, Statsig testing and first-party Segment tagging sit behind it.
section_summaries.retention: A Segment-to-Amplitude data stack and a 429-page help centre support a very large, low-touch user base, while the pricing page upsells Notetaker and Callie and recent customer stories appear to be doing the same. Churn figures are unknown.
section_summaries.content_strategy: The blog has become a product-announcement channel publishing roughly 13 posts in eight months, while its search traffic still comes from generic calendar and productivity guides rather than the new posts. The one new bet is an AI-integration cluster positioning Calendly as the scheduling layer for ChatGPT, Claude and voice agents.
section_summaries.history: Calendly sold "Easy scheduling ahead" essentially unchanged from January 2025 to July 2026, then rewrote the homepage and pricing page in a single quarter around AI meeting management. The price card never moved — the new Plus tiers are where the increase went.
section_summaries.jobs: Hiring is pointed entirely at building the AI product, not at selling it: all 8 open roles sit in engineering, product and security, three of them named for AI work, and none in marketing, sales or support.
section_summaries.stack: A mature setup: Segment feeding Amplitude, Marketo for lead capture, Statsig for testing, Maze for research and Intercom for chat, with tracking proxied through first-party calendly.com subdomains.
section_summaries.ads: Paid looks like a small part of the mix. LinkedIn holds 11 ads over a year split between team-focused product creative, a "How I Work" video series and recruitment; Meta has no active ads and no Calendly advertiser was found in Google's library despite a Google Ads tag on every page.
section_summaries.content_footprint: A 1,073-URL site dominated by support rather than marketing: 429 help pages and 287 blog posts, plus integration pages, resources and customer stories. The August–October 2026 lastmod spike most likely reflects the sitewide relaunch rather than new publishing.
section_summaries.search: Search is Calendly's biggest measurable channel and its most concentrated risk: the homepage alone takes 73% of estimated traffic across the top 100 pages, 69% of top-keyword traffic is branded, and the blog contributes 3%. Square, Zapier and Setmore are the real non-branded rivals.
